findings: Field, seating bowl, roof supports and surrounding neighborhood remain aligned with the reference. No displaced geometry or conspicuous stale image trail appears in this sampled frame.
Reconstruction visibly reduces noise on grass and broad roof/facade surfaces. The irregular field boundary and main seating tiers remain clear.
Residual low-sample grain and some softening/blotchy shading remain in the dense shaded seat rows and roof-edge shadows. This is not a claim of reference-level fine-detail reconstruction.
The lit playing field, white lighting frames and blue screen retain their reference placement and color. Field lighting remains separated from the dark roof and surrounding city.
Reconstruction reduces bright stochastic speckles across the grass and dark surfaces without a conspicuous new bright halo or smear in this sampled frame.
A few low-sample points and dark-seat noise remain. The near scoreboard back naturally occupies part of the lower edge in this aerial route; it does not block the intended field view.

limits: The visual review covers one final sampled frame per lighting mode at640x400; still comparisons cannot establish temporal behavior throughout a route.
The quantitative tests use32frames,8currentSPP and independent128SPP references, measured after warmup; image and temporal errors strictly improve for both cases.
Dense shaded rows remain noisy/soft at8SPP. The scene is an authored architectural reconstruction, not a surveyed seat inventory or exact game lighting reproduction.
Full movie encoding, captions, pacing and playback require the separate final-media checks. No GPU work was dispatched for this review.
